title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes
content:
Back-of-the-envelope notes — pricing / packaging (scratchpad)
Owner: Noah Patel (ctto: Priya, Ethan)
Dates: initial 2026-03-02, iter 2026-03-04
Status: very rough, questions + numbers to sanity-check with infra finance

Goals:
- Get quick unit economics for hosted API per token and per request (chat convos).
- Rough tier ideas (free / dev / scale / enterprise) + committed/reserved pricing for Dedicated.
- Embeddings vs generation separation and conversion math.

Assumptions (need to verify with infra & finance):
- Average generation mix: 70% text-gen (streaming), 30% embeddings/rerank. (placeholder)
- Average token length per response: 150 tokens out (50 tokens in prompt) => 200 net tokens per call (generation).
- Per-request overhead (control plane, prefix KV lookups, routing): ~0.5ms equiv CPU/GPU cost — small but non-zero.
- GPU perf targets (for cost amortization): rtx-a800-ish equiv? Use $3.50/hr (effective fully loaded) as placeholder for cloud-managed instance (this is not reserved Dedicated price). Finance to confirm.
- Inference throughput: ~2M tokens/hr per GPU for typical 3B-13B-ish quantized models with batching/continuous-kv (wild guess).
- Embeddings throughput (dense model) higher: ~10M tokens/hr per GPU equivalent.

Quick cost math (hosted):
- If 2M tokens/hr per GPU, cost per token = $3.50 / 2,000,000 = $0.00000175/token = $0.00175 per 1000 tokens.
- If average call = 200 tokens => cost per call = 200 * $0.00000175 = $0.00035 (~0.035 cents).
- Add infra + control plane + storage + SRE amortization: multiply by overhead factor 2.5 => all-in cost per 1k tokens ~= $0.004375 (~$0.0044/1k).
- Apply margin target (hosted) of 60% gross => list price per 1k tokens = cost / (1 - margin) => $0.004375 / 0.4 = $0.0109375 => ~$0.011/1k tokens.

Sanity check vs market: many providers at $0.03-$0.06 per 1k for similar models; our $0.011 looks aggressive but plausible if our perf assumptions hold. If GPU effective cost is higher ($10/hr) and throughput lower (1M tokens/hr), all-in cost per 1k becomes ~ $0.0125 and list price at 60% margin => $0.031. So sensitivity is large.

Embeddings math (separate SKU):
- If embeddings throughput 10M tokens/hr and same $3.50/hr => cost per token = $3.50/10M = $0.00000035/token = $0.00035 per 1k tokens.
- Many embedding APIs price per 1k vectors; convert: if average text -> 1 vector per request (e.g., chunking later), cost per 1k vectors ~ $0.00035. After overhead factor 2.5 => $0.000875/1k vectors. With 60% margin => $0.0022/1k vectors.
- Market prices for embeddings often $0.004-$0.02/1k vectors depending on model; again variance.

Tier sketches (hosted API):
- Free: 0 - 100k tokens/month free (dev/test). Hard tradeoff: free attracts misuse. Consider 30-50k tokens + rate limits.
- Starter (pay-as-you-go): $0.012/1k tokens (list) — no commitment; aimed at small apps / prototypes. Includes limited throughput and 7-day retention of logs.
- Pro: $0.008/1k tokens with $500/month minimum or $X tokens included (e.g., 50M tokens included) — priority support + higher throughput (better batching).
- Scale / Business: $0.0045/1k tokens with commit (monthly/annual) for 1–5M tokens/mo, SLA. Add feature flags: private model pinning, longer retention.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: custom pricing; reserved capacity (Dedicated) priced as committed vCPU/GPU + software platform fee.

Dedicated pricing sketch (reserved capacity):
- Goal: sell committed GPU months with discount vs hosted list. Example calc: if a Dedicated GPU fully loaded cost (hardware + ops + margin) = $6k/month (placeholder), and expected throughput is 60B tokens/month => effective base cost per 1k tokens = $0.0001. Then we can price reserved tokens at $0.001/1k (10x) with support/management. Need actual numbers from SRE/infra.
- Bundling: charge for min commit (e.g., 1 GPU for 3 months) + per-token overage at hosted list price * 0.75.

Unit economics for canary fallbacks / model variants:
- If we route to smaller cheaper model on fallback, we need clear equivalent price mapping. Provide per-request unit-profile: {latency SLO, mean tokens, cost multiplier}. Keep simple mapping table in product later.

Pricing levers we control (product):
- Batching aggressiveness / burst windows => affects throughput/cost per token (we should productize batch-level tiers: dev vs pro where pro allows higher batching for efficiency).
- KV cache / prefix caching => reduces tokens billed for repeated contexts? (billing still per token, but effective cost to us falls) Could offer cache-credits as upsell.
- Quantized model families => price differentiation by model family (fast-quant) vs high-quality (fp16).
- Reserved capacity discounts for Dedicated customers.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Verify actual tokens/hr per GPU for our common recommended models (3B, 7B, 13B, 70B) — ask serving-runtime team. (INF-501)
- Get fully loaded hourly cost for managed GPU vs Dedicated hardware (Finance/Infra).
- Decide margin targets by product line (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Current placeholder 60% for hosted. Is that realistic? Ask CFO.
- Decide free tier size — tradeoff growth vs abuse. Might gate by verified email + incremental quota.
- How to bill streaming responses vs per-token? For streaming we still bill per token but we might add per-request metadata cost for long-lived connections — need infra input.
- Embedding billing unit: per vector vs per token? Most customers expect per-vector. Need clear conversion guidelines for chunking.

Quick examples (to illustrate end-customer cost):
- Chat app with 1M monthly tokens: at $0.011/1k => $11/month (starter). At $0.0045/1k committed => $4.50/month.
- Agent orchestration heavy (10M tokens/mo): starter => $110/mo, Pro (0.008) => $80/mo, Scale committed => $45/mo.

Notes on commercial approach:
- PLG funnel: offer free trial credits (e.g., $50 = ~4.5M tokens at $0.011/1k) to encourage building.
- Marketplace listings: list hosted prices clearly; enterprise page: contact for Dedicated/private pricing.
- Use usage tier promos to drive commitment (e.g., commit 6 months => extra 10% discount).

Communication / docs to create next:
- Short internal memo summarizing assumptions + ask list for infra/finance. (link to PRIC-342).
- Calculator spreadsheet (sheet) that takes GPU hr cost, tokens/hr and outputs list price for given margin — share with Priya/Ethan.
- Draft product page copy for hosted API pricing (simple table + brief notes on committed/dedicated).

Immediate actions (next 1 week):
- Ping serving-runtime: actual tokens/hr per GPU by model family (3B, 7B, 13B, 70B) — @infra (INF-501).
- Get fully loaded cloud GPU/hr costs from finance (spot/ondemand/reserved).
- Build quick spreadsheet and sanity-check with current market comps.

Random scribbles / heuristics to remember:
- If we can increase batching by 2x without hurting latency SLO for non-interactive calls, cost per token halves. Product can expose batching controls.
- Embeddings are lucrative low-cost SKU; make sure to separate quotas and rate limits.
- Dedicated should be framed as "predictable throughput + lower unit cost + data isolation". Price as premium for ops + support rather than purely hardware.

End notes: this is intentionally messy. Will refine after numbers from infra/finance.

-- Noah
